mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 650i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a BMW 650i, replacement costs vary significantly by generation. E63 650i (N62B48) engines range from £1,800-£3,200 used, £3,200-£5,500 reconditioned, and £4,500-£7,000 rebuilt. F06/F12/F13 650i (N63B44) engines are more expensive: £3,500-£6,000 used, £6,000-£10,000 reconditioned, and £8,000-£14,000 rebuilt (N63B44O0) or £5,000-£9,000 used, £9,000-£14,000 reconditioned, and £12,000-£18,000 rebuilt (N63B44T). Labour adds approximately £1,000-£1,500 for specialist fitment.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of valve stem seal failure in a BMW 650i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common telltale sign is blue smoke from the exhaust, particularly on startup or after idling. You may also notice excessive oil consumption requiring frequent top-ups between services. The problem occurs when the rubber valve stem seals harden and crack with age, allowing oil to seep into the combustion chamber. This affects both N62 (E63) and N63 (F-generation) 650i engines.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 650i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and value. For an E63 650i worth under £5,000, consider repair or a used engine rather than a full rebuild. For F-generation 650is worth £8,000-£15,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For 650is worth £15,000+, replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. If the car is otherwise in excellent condition, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components can extend its life by 80,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 650i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 650i engine replacements take 2-4 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The V8 engine's complexity - particularly on N63 twin-turbo units - means careful removal and installation is essential. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 6 Series 650i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 650i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with 3-6 month warranties, while reconditioned units usually include 6-12 month cover. Extended warranty options are available on most rebuilt units.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N62 and N63 engines in the BMW 650i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N62 is a 4.8-litre naturally aspirated V8 producing 367hp, fitted to E63/E64 650is from 2005-2010. The N63 is a 4.4-litre twin-turbocharged V8 producing 407hp (2011-2014) or 450hp (2014-2018), fitted to F06/F12/F13 650is. The N63 is significantly more powerful but also more complex, with additional failure points including turbochargers, high-pressure fuel pumps, and timing chain issues not present on the N62.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 650i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 650i debuted in 2005 as the V8 flagship of the second-generation E63/E64 6 Series, replacing the 645Ci. Over its production life across two generations, the 650i evolved from a naturally aspirated 4.8-litre V8 to a twin-turbo 4.4-litre V8, with a significant power hike at the 2014 facelift.

N63B44O0, 4.4L twin-turbo V8, 407hp - F12 convertible and F13 coupe launch
N63B44O0, 407hp - F06 Gran Coupe added to range
N63B44T, 4.4L twin-turbo V8, 450hp - LCI facelift across F06/F12/F13

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 650i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 650i's N62 and N63 V8 engines deliver exceptional performance but are among the more complex petrol engines to maintain. N62-powered E63/E64 650is (2005-2010) suffer primarily from valve stem seal degradation and cooling system failures, while N63-powered F06/F12/F13 650is (2011-2018) add turbocharger, timing chain and fuel injector issues to the list. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Excessive Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Failure
problems.h4: Excessive Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the BMW 6 Series 650i N62/N63 Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The rubber valve stem seals harden and crack with age and heat exposure, losing their ability to seal the valve guide. Oil seeps into the combustion chamber and burns, producing blue smoke from the exhaust. This problem carried over from the N62 to the N63 engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all valve stem seals (labour-intensive; cylinder head access required)
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if engine otherwise healthy and vehicle worth £8,000+

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best for higher-mileage units with multiple concurrent failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E63/E64 650i (2005-2010) is worth £4,000-£12,000, with many examples under £6,000. A typical F06/F12/F13 650i (2011-2018) is worth £8,000-£22,000. For E63 650is valued under £5,000, a valve stem seal repair may be more sensible than a full rebuilt engine. For F-generation 650is valued £8,000-£15,000, reconditioned/rebuilt replacement usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For 650is valued £15,000+, replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your 650i has valve stem seal wear but the engine is otherwise healthy and the car has strong value, specialist seal replacement is a cost-effective fix. If the engine has multiple concurrent failures - valve stem seals, timing chain wear, and turbocharger issues on N63 cars - a rebuilt engine with upgraded components is often the better long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N63B44 BMW 6 Series 650i engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - BMW 6 Series 650i N63 Engine
problems.rootCause: The timing chain stretches or the timing chain guides fail, causing the engine's valves to lose synchronisation with the pistons. Symptoms include rattling noises from the engine on cold starts, rough idling, and the Check Engine Light illuminating. If left unchecked, a failed timing chain can cause catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early and engine otherwise sound

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain failure has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. For F-generation 650is, timing chain replacement is typically viable if the car is worth over £8,000.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling on cold start, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Early replacement of the chain and guides can save the engine. If the chain has already failed causing internal damage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the only reliable solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N63B44T BMW 6 Series 650i engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - BMW 6 Series 650i N63 Twin-Turbo
problems.rootCause: Heat generated by the turbos causes premature wear of turbocharger bearings. Oil supply line blockage starves the turbos of lubrication. Wastegate actuators can also develop issues, causing rattling noises and inconsistent boost delivery.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed turbocharger unit, inspect oil supply
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one turbo failed and oil system clear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded turbo components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if both turbos failing or engine has other issues

problems.recommendation: Turbocharger failure on an N63 650i often signals broader engine health issues. If one turbo has failed, have the oil supply system thoroughly inspected - blockage here can kill the replacement turbo too. If both turbos are failing or the engine has other issues, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components is the safer long-term choice.
